title: The 7 Best Dovetail Saw 2026
metaDescription: Our 7 picks for dovetail saw 2026, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at dovetail saw 2026 using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: Crown 188 8-Inch Dovetail Saw with Full Handle
products.blurb: Key specs: 20 TPI, Brass back, Full rosewood handle.
strengths: Resharpenable high carbon steel blade lasts far longer than impulse-hardened alternatives
Full rosewood handle gives excellent control for beginners and experienced hands alike
Made in Sheffield with a reputation for quality well above its price point
limitations: Resharpening eventually requires sending the blade to a professional sharpening service
Slightly less refined fit and finish than premium hand-filed saws
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Gyokucho Razorsaw Dovetail Saw 240mm No. 311
products.blurb: Key specs: Pull-stroke cutting, Replaceable blade, Very fine teeth.
strengths: Pull-stroke cutting puts the blade in tension, allowing an extremely thin, accurate kerf without buckling
Replaceable blade avoids the cost and skill of resharpening entirely
Very fine tooth count leaves an exceptionally clean cut with minimal tearout
limitations: Pull-saw technique takes adjustment for woodworkers used to Western push saws
Blade replacement is an ongoing cost rather than a one-time purchase

products.name: Stanley Fatmax 15-252K 10-Inch Dovetail Saw with Reversible Handle
products.blurb: Key specs: 13 TPI, Reversible offset handle, Stiff steel back.
strengths: Very low price for a first dovetail saw to learn technique on
Reversible handle allows flush cuts left or right without buying a second saw
Compact size suits smaller box and drawer joinery
limitations: Blade flexes more than premium saws, harder to track a straight line
Handle comfort noticeably below premium options during extended use
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Two Cherries 520-6020 10-Inch Brass Back Dovetail Saw
products.blurb: Key specs: 15 TPI rip filed, Solid brass back, German steel blade.
strengths: Solid brass back adds mass and rigidity that keeps the cut tracking true
German-made blade holds an edge well through repeated dovetail cutting
Longstanding reputation among furniture makers for exceptional quality at a reasonable price
limitations: Ships with a moderate factory edge; some buyers touch it up before first use
Traditional handle shape takes some adjustment for those used to modern ergonomic grips
products.bestFor: buyers who want the best overall package

products.name: Silky WOODBOY 384-24 240mm X-Fine Dozuki Saw
products.blurb: Key specs: X-fine impulse-hardened teeth, Folding blade design, Rigid steel back.
strengths: Folding design protects the blade and makes storage safer than an open-back saw
Impulse-hardened X-fine teeth hold an edge through repeated dovetail work
Good balance of price and cutting performance for an intermediate woodworker
limitations: Impulse-hardened teeth cannot be resharpened, saw is replaced once dull
Pull-stroke technique takes adjustment for woodworkers used to push saws

products.name: Robert Larson 300 Dozuki Saw with Replaceable Blade
products.blurb: Key specs: Pull-stroke cutting, Replaceable blade, Fine crosscut and rip teeth.
strengths: Very sharp out of the box, cuts cleanly with minimal setup
Replaceable blade keeps ongoing cost predictable and low
Good introduction to pull-saw technique at a lower price than Gyokucho
limitations: Blade is thinner and more prone to kinking if forced
Handle wrap can loosen over time and needs occasional retightening
products.bestFor: value-focused buyers who want the most for their money

products.name: Shark Corp 10-2204 Dowel/Dovetail/Detail Saw
products.blurb: Key specs: 24 TPI, Interchangeable blade, Very narrow kerf.
strengths: Very narrow kerf and fine tooth count leave a clean line on tight dovetail work
Interchangeable blade keeps the saw cutting sharp without a full replacement
Flexible blade also handles flush-trimming dowels and plugs
limitations: No back spine, less rigid than a brass or steel-backed saw
Not as refined a cutting feel as Veritas or Lie-Nielsen

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
